title: Pocket Pitlane
user: Friends with one shared TV or laptop who want a five-minute competitive racing game where every phone is a controller and nobody installs an app.

evidence.quote_or_summary: In feedback on a browser racer, an HN commenter says 'we need more games in this space'; another explicitly asks for browser controllers for schools, while several report confusing phone/room-code onboarding.
The fetched live page identifies Sim Drive as a multiplayer racing simulator with phone controllers, demonstrating the desired zero-install play surface.

recurrence: One 2026 thread contains independent demand for more phone-controlled browser games plus repeated join-flow failures; the pain is acute when a group is standing around a screen.
current_workaround: Use Jackbox-style paid packs, pass a keyboard around, or make everyone install a mobile game.
incumbents_and_gap: Jackbox, AirConsole, SimDrive, and PadlessBox prove the format, but the shared friction is setup: QR loops, unclear host-versus-controller roles, and small game collections. A single polished arcade race can remove that first-minute failure mode.
smallest_useful_product: A 2-8 player top-down race: host creates a six-character room on the big screen, phones open a controller link, and a 90-second race begins after a visual ready check. Runs vary through rotating track hazards and one drafted power. Non-goals: accounts, voice chat, physics simulation, or a party-game platform.
success_measure: At least 70% of new rooms start a race with two or more controllers within 90 seconds, and 35% play a second race in the same visit.
monetization: free — a frictionless room link is the product; sponsorship or a paid cosmetic track pack can be tested only after retention exists.
constraints: Use WebSockets with region-aware relay; request device-motion permission only after an explicit tap and provide touch steering; collect no phone identity or contact data.
why_distinct: It is a single purpose-built, setup-proof couch race, not another collection of licensed party prompts or a controller SDK.
